next_step: Run one prospective held-out benchmark within the promised family. Before seeing results, set a common cost metric and freeze the workload. Compare the learned scaffold with the strongest conventional baseline using the same thin representation; record acquisition/preparation cost and per-task cost separately, then calculate the reuse count needed to break even.

allocation.worker_1: Measure acquisition and preparation cost in the predeclared metric.
allocation.worker_2: Profile both implementations on the frozen workload in the same environment; report wall time and arithmetic counts separately.

decisive_observation: Whether the learned scaffold’s measured per-task savings over the equally informed conventional baseline repay its acquisition/preparation cost at a plausible reuse count.

outcome_decisions.savings repay cost: Retain the representation and test transfer on another held-out task.
outcome_decisions.no savings or implausible break-even: Keep the algebraic result, but stop claiming a total-cost learning advantage for this scaffold.
outcome_decisions.same thin representation benefits both e: Use the simpler conventional implementation; retain the thin representation only where it helps.

retained_result: The seven-point agreement validates the reported outputs at those replay points; the interpreter counts show higher arithmetic use there. Neither establishes wall-time or future-workload performance.
uncertainty: One prospective workload cannot establish cross-family generalization; cost weights and plausible reuse count need justification.
